title: Longest Run With No Shared Bits
statement:
You get an array of positive integers nums. Call a contiguous subarray clean if no two of its elements share a set bit, that is, a & b = 0 for every pair of different positions in it, not only neighbours.

Return the length of the longest clean subarray. A single element is always clean.

examples.why: [1, 2, 4] is clean, but 3 shares a bit with both 1 and 2. [4, 3, 8, 16] uses bits 2, 0–1, 3 and 4, which never overlap.
Equal numbers always share their bits, so only single elements are clean.
Each neighbouring pair is fine, but the two 1s share bit 0, so the whole array is not clean.

hints: Since every pair in a clean window must have no common bit, what can you say about the OR of the whole window?
A new number can join a clean window exactly when it shares no bit with the OR of the window. Keep that OR as a running mask.
Slide a window. When the next number collides with the mask, drop numbers from the left, removing their bits from the mask with XOR, until it fits.

explain.intuition:
In a clean window no bit is used twice, so each bit of the OR belongs to exactly one element. That gives a cheap summary: one integer used holding all the bits in the window. A new number fits exactly when used & x == 0.

And because bits are owned by one element each, removing the leftmost element is just used ^= nums[lo]: its bits are switched off without touching anyone else's. This is a normal sliding window, with the bitmask playing the role of a "seen" set. A clean window can hold at most 30 numbers, since there are only 30 bits below 109.
steps: For each hi, while used & nums[hi] is not 0, do used ^= nums[lo] and lo++.
pitfalls: Checking only adjacent pairs. In [1, 2, 1] the conflict is between the ends.
Removing an element with used &= ~x or ^= before it is known that bits are unique. It is only safe because the window is clean.
Restarting the window at hi after a conflict. The conflict may be with an early element only, so part of the window can stay (see the first example).

solutions.title: Extend from every start
solutions.idea: From each start, keep adding elements while they do not collide with the OR so far. A clean run has at most 30 elements, so each start costs at most about 30 steps.

solutions.title: Sliding window with a bit mask
solutions.idea: Keep the OR of a clean window. On a collision, XOR elements out from the left until the new number fits.

followups: Each bit may now be shared by at most two elements of the window. What do you keep instead of a single mask?
Count how many clean subarrays there are in total, not just the longest.
